The digest misplaces Dorothy's collapse: she threw herself on the bed when two men ran up to say the service was over, and lay there until Sara Hutchinson said the party was coming. It also fails to say that the ring passage is the struck-through text, absent from Knight's 1897 edition (which prints the rest of the entry).

fix.digest: Dorothy wrote the wedding entry later. She did not go to the church. Before the couple set out she gave William the wedding ring, which she had worn overnight; he slipped it back onto her finger and blessed her. These lines were later struck through by an unknown hand and are missing from Knight's 1897 text. When two men ran up the walk to say the service was over, she threw herself on her bed and lay still until Sara Hutchinson came to say they were coming, then went out to meet William, and he and John Hutchinson led her into the house. After breakfast the three set off in the rain for Grasmere.
fix.source_note: Grasmere journal, 4 Oct 1802 (DCMS 31); full text including the struck-through lines in Woof, The Grasmere Journals (1991); Knight (1897) prints the entry without the ring passage.
